sections.html:
McIntosh County is in east central Oklahoma, with Eufaula as its seat. It covers 712 square miles, and 13 percent of that is water, mostly Eufaula Lake, the largest reservoir wholly inside the state. The 2020 Census counted 18,941 residents and 11,755 housing units. Here is the number sellers should notice: 32.4 percent of those units were vacant. Owners live in 78.6 percent of the occupied homes, and the median age is 49.5, with 26.9 percent of residents 65 or older.

Checotah and Eufaula are the cities. Hanna, Hitchita, Rentiesville, Stidham and Vernon are towns, and Duchess Landing, Shady Grove and Texanna are census-designated places. Interstate 40 and US 69 cross the county, along with US 266, State Highways 9 and 72 and the Indian Nation Turnpike. Most of the county lies inside the Muscogee (Creek) Nation and the far east inside the Cherokee Nation. County property tax is billed the same way in both.

The assessor values property and files the roll. The treasurer collects. Both jobs follow the state pattern, and you will deal with each at different points in a sale.

OfficeContactWhat you do there
Assessor918-689-2611Valuation questions, homestead and other exemptions, mailing address updates
Treasurer110 North First Street, Eufaula, OK 74432, 918-689-2491, Monday to Friday, 8:00 AM to 4:00 PMPayments by mail, in the office, in the drop box on the south side of the courthouse, or online by credit card

The treasurer's page links to the assessor's ACTDataScout site, where you can find parcels and values. Start at the treasurer page or the assessor page.

sections.h2: How a tax bill is built
sections.html:
After the Excise Board sets millage, the assessor certifies the roll. One combined statement then goes out covering the county, cities and towns, and schools. A mill equals $1 on each $1,000 of taxable value, and assessment ratios across Oklahoma run 10 to 15 percent.

A primary home gets $1,000 knocked off taxable value through the homestead exemption, and its assessed value cannot rise more than 3 percent in a year unless it sells. Lake-area second homes miss out on the homestead deduction, since it covers only a primary residence.

  • Value: assessor.
  • Levies: each taxing body, certified by the Excise Board.
  • Collection: treasurer.

sections.h2: Due dates, interest and new-owner steps
sections.html:
This county asks for half by December 31 and the balance by March 31. Skip that December half and January 1 turns the entire bill delinquent. Only balances above $25 may be split, and no reminder for the second half is mailed to you, so write the March date down.

  • Late tax costs 18 percent yearly, applied as 1.5 percent each month on the 16th.
  • A statement that never reached you is not a legal ground for forgiving interest.
  • New owners should give the assessor a mailing address before September 30, ahead of the date accounts are certified to the treasurer.
  • Mortgage companies often pay through a tax service, so a paid bill can take time to appear.
  • All delinquent years must be paid at the same time. You cannot skip one.

A personal lien on a property can also hold up a mortgage company's payment until the lien is satisfied.

Exemption paperwork, homestead included, belongs at the assessor's desk and never the treasurer's. The homestead break takes $1,000 off taxable value, but only for the house where the owner actually lives. A rental or weekend lake cabin is out. Whoever buys and moves in must apply for themselves once the purchase is done, so do not promise a buyer that your exemption transfers. Ask the assessor how a vacant house is classified if yours has been empty.

Put your objection in writing and deliver it to the assessor. The window is 30 calendar days counted from the mailing date on a notice of higher value, or the first Monday in April when the number is unchanged.

The assessor hears you informally and answers on paper within 7 calendar days. Beyond that you can go to the county board of equalization, with 15 days to do it. The assessor drives by every property on a four-year visual inspection schedule, so a recent drive-by can explain why a value moved. Ask what was observed, and bring photos if the notes are wrong, such as an outbuilding that no longer stands or a roof you replaced.

Taxes owed are settled at closing out of your sale proceeds, so ask the treasurer for a current payoff. Because all delinquent years have to be paid together, ask for the full list of years rather than just the latest one.

  1. Ask the treasurer for a written payoff that includes every delinquent year.
  2. Ask the assessor to confirm the parcel's mailing address and classification.
  3. Ask the title company to check for liens before you accept a price.
  4. Confirm that a mortgage servicer's tax service actually paid before assuming the bill is cleared.

If you are listing in winter, one more step helps: the treasurer cannot accept a first-half payment after December 31, so find out early whether that half is in.

sections.h2: Selling a lake-area or rural house
sections.html:
Eufaula Lake shaped the local housing market. The lake was finished in 1964 and brought boat building, tourism and retail, and many of the houses buyers look at now are either lake-area homes or older farm and ranch properties. A buyer's lender and insurer will ask about storm damage, the age of the roof and anything that touches the water line, so gather that history before the first showing.

Vacancy is high in this county, so a house that has sat empty is not unusual. Buyers will still ask why. Be ready to explain how long it has been vacant, who has kept the utilities and yard in shape, and whether taxes stayed current while nobody lived there.

The usual seller owns an older rural house, a lake-area property, an inherited home or a house that has been empty for a while. With about 27 percent of residents 65 or older, estate sales and downsizing are common reasons.

Lakefront homes, aging rural houses and inherited properties all show up, and many need repairs that a retail buyer's lender would not accept. A cash purchase as-is avoids lender-driven repair demands. If back taxes, a probate or a vacant house is the issue, a straight payoff figure first lets you compare options sensibly. An empty house is also worth a call to the assessor to learn how the parcel is classified.

Keep the parcel number, your latest statement, any valuation notice and the deed or probate papers near the phone whenever you talk to the treasurer, the assessor or a buyer. It saves repeat calls and speeds up an offer.

Land inside tribal jurisdictions can raise parcel-specific questions, so ask the title company about the details of your parcel before you list or sign.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a McIntosh County valuation?
faqs.a: Valuation is the County Assessor's job. Dial 918-689-2611.

faqs.q: When are McIntosh County property taxes due?
faqs.a: Half by December 31, the rest by March 31. Miss the December date and the full bill is delinquent.

faqs.q: What interest does McIntosh County charge on late property tax?
faqs.a: The treasurer adds 1.5 percent on the 16th of every month, equal to 18 percent a year.

faqs.q: Where do I file a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: File it with the County Assessor. The treasurer does not take exemption applications.

faqs.q: Do I need to report a new address after buying?
faqs.a: Yes. Give the assessor your mailing address before September 30, ahead of certification to the treasurer, so the statement finds you.
